title: Kanssa with several companions
summary: Put a plural genitive before kanssa (“with”): lasten kanssa (“with the children”).
prerequisiteSkills: Location postpositions with a singular genitive
objectives: Put a plural genitive before kanssa (“with”): lasten kanssa (“with the children”).

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Kanssa follows the companion expression: genitive noun/name + kanssa. It does not come before the noun as English “with” does.
Companion models: lapsi → lasten/lapsien, ystävä → ystävien, opettaja → opettajien, opiskelija → opiskelijoiden/opiskelijoitten.
The supplied verb frames are Olen (“I am”) and Tulen (“I come/am coming”). Personal-pronoun combinations with kanssa have additional written-Finnish forms and are outside this lesson.

steps: Use lasten before kanssa. The companion expression is a plural genitive; the speaker remains one person.

commonMistakes: Use the genitive form of the noun or name.
The companion's number does not change the supplied first-person verb.
